title: trace-sprint-wrap-ops-notes-2026-09-03
content:
Week-of 2026-09-03 — Observability: trace sprint wrap + dashboard pruning experiment

Attendees: Maya Patel (owner), Ethan Kim, Riley Chen, Lena Garcia, Noah Brooks, guest: Priya Singh (SRE)

Purpose: wrap up the 2-week trace-cost sprint, capture outcomes from the sampling and dashboard rationalization experiments, and list operational actions we need to carry into the next cycle. This doc is intentionally conversational — notes from the sync and quick standup captures.

High-level outcome
- Reduced overall span volume by ~38% for the HTTP frontends without losing top-1 latency signals. That reduction maps to a measured 17% lower ingestion bill in our trace ingestion vendor for the test pool.
- Dashboard pruning pilot: out of 42 candidate dashboards we instrumented for usage telemetry, 27 have <4 views/week. We will archive 18 of those and merge the remaining 9 into consolidated views.
- Sampling policy prototype (prefix + error-weighted) is in demo-ready state; needs e2e runbook + canary config for 2% of production traffic.

This week — quick standup log (daily highlights)
- Mon 2026-09-01: final verified span dedupe heuristics for RPC fanout. Found a pathological 2.7x duplication in batch path; fixed by dedupe key change (service+trace_id+op_index). Deployed to test region.
- Tue 2026-09-02: dashboard telemetry collectors shipped (backfill enabled, 7d retention). Early data shows 40% of dashboard loads are ad-hoc from SRE alerts.
- Wed 2026-09-03: run sampling experiment A/B on trace volume for frontend traffic: baseline vs error-biased sampling (retain all errors, 1-in-4 on success). Observed no change in alert fidelity for P95/P99 latency on test endpoints.
- Thu 2026-09-04: cost-backfill reconciliation with finance; preliminary estimate: sampling + dedupe should save ~$7k monthly on ingestion for the two larger services. Need firm numbers after full-week run.
- Fri 2026-09-05: walkthrough of canary playbook with SRE and on-call. Action: add explicit rollback trigger when diagnostic dashboards show >5% delta in error capture for canary slice.

Deep dives / experiment notes
1) Span-sampling experiment (error-weighted + prefix retention)\   - Design: keep 100% of spans with status >= 400, keep all spans for requests that hit our critical prefixes (/api/v2/payments, /api/v2/agreements), sample success traces at 1:4 by default.\   - Metric targets: reduce span volume by 30-50% with <2% degradation in high-level alert signals (P95/P99 latency, error-rate).\   - Results (72h): overall span count reduced 38%; error capture remained at 100% for monitored errors; synthetic trace injection test showed no missed alerts across 12 scenarios.\   - Observed risk: secondary heatmap for cold-starts (first request of container) lost some distribution resolution for a few rare endpoints. Plan: add a short full-retain window (first 10 minutes after container start).

2) Dashboard rationalization pilot\   - Approach: added lightweight telemetry to dashboard service (view count, owner, last-run from alerts). Flagged candidates: low-usage, high-cardinality dashboards that are expensive to render.\   - Decision: archive 18 dashboards, consolidate 9 into a new "ops-summary" dashboard, and move 6 into a slower-refresh archive-tier (1h).\   - Next: owner outreach template drafted (consolidation-notice.md) and a 10-day freeze before archive.

Operational notes / runbook updates needed
- Add a canary page to the runbook that lists the exact Linear IDs and Slack channel the canary posts to. Linked doc: linear RED-4821.
- Create a rollback metric: if error capture for canary slice < 95% of baseline or P95 latency delta > 5% then auto-rollback sampling change.
- Add an on-call checklist item: after sampling toggles, run quick-sanity script (repo: telemetry-config/scripts/quick-sanity.sh).

Action items (owner — due)
- Ethan Kim — finalize canary YAML + rollout percentages and commit to telemetry-config (due 2026-09-08).
- Riley Chen — draft the owner outreach messages and schedule a 1:1 with the top-5 owners of dashboards slated for archive (due 2026-09-07).
- Lena Garcia — compute full-month cost projection with finance using 30/38/45% saving scenarios, and provide a conservative forecast (due 2026-09-10).
- Noah Brooks — add container-start full-retention window code and add unit test for dedupe edge-case (due 2026-09-09).
- Maya Patel — author the "canary playbook" doc and point to rollback triggers; coordinate SRE review (due 2026-09-11).

Unresolved questions / discussion items
- What threshold defines "high-cardinality but useful" dashboard? Proposal: >200 uniques per 7d AND >1 alert target. Need feedback.
- Is 1:4 sampling for successes conservative enough for long-tail troubleshooting? Suggest we hold a 3-week observation window before increasing sampling ratio.
- How do we surface sampling changes to customers (internal platform consumers)? A simple header in trace UI and an entry in the change log? Ops thought: add a single-line TSV in the trace search that shows "sampling-status".

Follow-ups for next week
- Kick the 2% production canary for sampling on Monday (Ethan). Monitor the canary for 72h and escalate at any rollback signal.
- Start owner outreach for dashboards slated for archive (Riley).
- Full week cost reconciliation (Lena + Finance).
- Integrate the quick-sanity script into on-call runbook and add a Slack alert target for failures (Noah).

Notes to self / messy ideas to record
- Could we opportunistically use trace ingestion spikes to trigger temporal throttles (short-term backpressure) instead of global sampling toggles? Worth prototyping but needs careful SLA thinking.
- Long-term: consider an RLS-style retention per-tenant for traces used by customer-facing teams; low priority but high upside for cost allocation.

TL;DR: sampling + dedupe gave clear wins in test slices, dashboard pruning is low-friction and will cut render cost. Immediate focus: safe canary and owner communication.

If you want any of the raw experiment data (time-series exports, test traces), ping me and I'll drop a bucket link or the Linear ticket with attachments.
